professional [[basketball]] player for [[Olympiacos B.C.|Olympiacos]] of the [[Greek Basket League]] and the [[EuroLeague]].{{Cite web|url=https://fenerbahce.org/haberler/basketbol-erkek/2023/2/tyler-dorsey-fenerbahce-beko-da|title=Tyler Dorsey Fenerbahçe Beko'da - Fenerbahçe Spor Kulübü|website=Fenerbahce.org|access-date=August 14, 2026}} He is also a member of the [[Greece men's national basketball team|Greek national basketball team]], and plays at the [[shooting guard]] position. After graduating from [[Maranatha High School]] in [[Pasadena, California]], Dorsey played [[college basketball]] for the [[Oregon Ducks men's basketball|Oregon Ducks]]. An [[All-EuroLeague Team|All-EuroLeague Second Team]] selection in [[2025–26 EuroLeague|2025–26]], he reached three [[Euroleague Final Four|EuroLeague Final Fours]] with Olympiacos, winning the title in 2026. Dorsey has been a member of the [[Greek national basketball team|Greek national team]] since 2022. He helped Greece capture the bronze medal at [[EuroBasket 2025]]. ==High school career== Dorsey initially attended [[Ribét Academy]] in his freshman season. He then transferred to [[St. John Bosco High School]], in [[Bellflower, California]]. In his [[sophomore]] season, he began to establish himself as a solid scorer, with a 17.0 [[Point (basketball)|points]]-per-game scoring average. He made a big impact afterwards, where, as a [[Eleventh grade|junior]], he managed to help his team win the state championship, and was the star of the team, averaging 21.4 points per game, 6.0 [[Rebound (basketball)|rebounds]], and 4.7 [[Assist (basketball)|assists]] per game. In his senior year, he decided to transfer to [[Maranatha High School|Maranatha]], due to his desire to return to his hometown of [[Pasadena, California|Pasadena]]. While there, he averaged 34.0 [[Point (basketball)|points]] per game, to go along with 10.4 [[Rebound (basketball)|rebounds]], 3.7 [[Assist (basketball)|assists]], and 1.9 [[Steal (basketball)|steals]] per game. Together with his second state championship win, he earned the 2015 Gatorade State Player of the Year for [[California]] award. He had many impressive games, like the one where he scored 52 points, in an 85–60 win. He was able to be efficient in every game, shown by the fact that he finished in double figures in scoring all 30 of his games played. Despite being considered the 23rd-best player of his age group, he was not selected to play in the [[McDonald's All-American Game]]. He initially committed to play [[college basketball]] at the [[University of Arizona]], but he changed his mind, and then committed to [[University of Oregon|Oregon]], instead, on February 2, 2015. ==College career== ===Freshman year=== Dorsey played his first [[official game]] as an [[Oregon Ducks men's basketball|Oregon Duck]], in the season opener against [[Jackson State Tigers basketball|Jackson State]], where [[Oregon Ducks men's basketball|Oregon]] won; and he was declared the [[Most Valuable Player|MVP]] of the game, after scoring 20 [[Point (basketball)|points]] for his team, in an 80–52 win. Dorsey missed two games in the middle of the [[Season (sports)|season]], due to an [[injury]], but he soon came back into form. He scored a career-high 25 [[Point (basketball)|points]] against rivals [[Oregon State Beavers men's basketball|Oregon State]], in a 91–81 win. The [[Oregon Ducks men's basketball|Ducks]] won the [[Pac-12 Conference|Pac-12]] [[Season (sports)|regular season]] and [[2016 Pac-12 Conference men's basketball tournament|2016 Conference tournament]]. In the [[2016 Pac-12 Conference men's basketball tournament#Bracket|tournament final]] against the [[Utah Utes men's basketball|University Of Utah]], Dorsey's team, Oregon, dominated, and beat Utah by a score of 88–57. Oregon's 31-point margin of victory was the largest in the Pac-12 Championship game's history. Dorsey had a stellar performance, being the top scorer, with 23 points, and having also grabbed 9 [[Rebound (basketball)|rebounds]]. He was picked for the [[2016 Pac-12 Conference men's basketball tournament#All-tournament team|All-Tournament Team]], and was the tournament's top scorer. Oregon earned the top seed in the West region, and went as the number one team of their conference into [[March Madness 2016|March Madness]]. After the season, Dorsey was one out of 162 early-entry candidates that initially declared for the [[2016 NBA draft]].{{Cite web|url=http://registerguard.com/rg/sports/34310794-81/tyler-dorsey-dillon-brooks-officially-declare-for-nba-draft.html.csp|title=Tyler Dorsey, Dillon Brooks officially declare for NBA Draft.|website=Registerguard.com|access-date=August 14, 2026}} However, he ultimately withdrew before the draft withdrawal deadline.{{Cite web|url=https://www.oregonlive.com/ducks/2016/05/dillon_brooks_and_tyler_dorsey.html|title=Dillon Brooks and Tyler Dorsey withdraw from NBA Draft, return to Oregon Ducks|first=Tyson |last=Alger|date=May 25, 2016|website=The Oregonian}} ===Sophomore year=== Dorsey helped the [[Oregon Ducks men's basketball|Ducks]] to the finals of the [[2017 Pac-12 Conference men's basketball tournament|Pac-12 conference tournament]], and he was named to the [[2017 Pac-12 Conference men's basketball tournament#All-Tournament Team|All-Tournament Team]]. Later, in the [[2017 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]], Dorsey hit numerous shots down the stretch against the [[Rhode Island Rams men's basketball|University of Rhode Island]] and the [[Michigan Wolverines men's basketball|University of Michigan]], to lead his team to the [[2017 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament#Final Four|Final Four]]. Oregon was finally defeated by the eventual champions, the [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina Tar Heels]]. ==Professional career== ===Atlanta Hawks (2017–2019)=== Dorsey was selected by the [[Atlanta Hawks]], in the 2nd round of the [[2017 NBA draft]], with 41st overall pick of the draft. He then signed a 2-year contract with the Hawks.{{Cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/hawks/news/hawks-sign-second-round-pick-tyler-dorsey|title=Hawks Sign Second-Round Pick Tyler Dorsey|website=Atlanta Hawks}} On November 12, 2017, Dorsey was sent by Atlanta to the [[Erie BayHawks (2017–)|Erie BayHawks]], of the [[NBA G League]], on assignment.{{cite web|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/hawks-tyler-dorsey-assigned-to-g-league/|title=Hawks' Tyler Dorsey: Assigned to G-League|work=CBSSports.com|date=November 12, 2017|access-date=November 12, 2017}} ===Memphis Grizzlies (2019)=== On February 7, 2019, Dorsey was traded to the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] in exchange for [[Shelvin Mack]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/memphis-grizzlies-acquire-tyler-dorsey-atlanta-hawks|title=Memphis Grizzlies acquire Tyler Dorsey from Atlanta Hawks |publisher=National Basketball Association|date=February 7, 2019|access-date=February 8, 2019}} He was assigned to the [[Memphis Hustle]] on February 8 and made his debut that evening. By the end of the 2018–19 season, Dorsey was regularly playing crunch-time minutes for the Grizzlies. ===Maccabi Tel Aviv (2019–2021)=== On August 17, 2019, Dorsey joined [[Maccabi Tel Aviv B.C.|Maccabi Tel Aviv]] of the [[Israeli Basketball Premier League|Israeli Premier League]] and the [[EuroLeague]], signing a one-year deal with an option for another one.{{cite web|url=http://maccabi.co.il/news.asp?id=7215|title=מכבי החתימה את טיילר דורסי|work=maccabi.co.il|date=August 17, 2019|access-date=August 17, 2019|language=he}} On November 1, 2019, Dorsey recorded a (basketball)|Fenerbahçe]] in 2023]] ===Fenerbahçe (2023–2024)=== On March 1, 2023, Dorsey signed with Turkish powerhouse [[Fenerbahçe S.K. (basketball)|Fenerbahçe]] through 2025, joining his Greek national team coach [[Dimitrios Itoudis]], as well as his teammates [[Nick Calathes]] and [[Kostas Antetokounmpo]].{{cite web |last1=Yahyabeyoglu |first1=Fersu |title=Fenerbahce tabs Tyler Dorsey |url=https://www.eurobasket.com/Euroleague/news/796107/Fenerbahce-tabs-Tyler-Dorsey |website=Eurobasket |access-date=March 1, 2023 |date=March 1, 2023}} ===Return to Olympiacos (2024–present)=== On June 30, 2024, Dorsey signed a three-year contract with [[Olympiacos B.C.|Olympiacos]], returning to the club after two seasons. ==National team career== ===Greek junior national team=== [[File:Tyler Dorsey.jpg|thumb|Dorsey, with the [[Greece men's national under-19 basketball team|Greek Under-19 national team]], during the [[2015 FIBA Under-19 World Championship|2015 FIBA Under-19 World Cup.]]]] Dorsey was originally cut from a [[USA Basketball]] tryout camp for its [[USA national under-19 basketball team|Under-18 national team]] in 2014. The next year, before the [[2015 FIBA Under-19 World Championship|2015 FIBA Under-19 World Cup]] began, he was invited to [[Greece men's national under-19 basketball team|Greece's Under-19 national team]] tryout camp, for which he was eligible due to his mother's Greek family.{{Cite magazine |last=Winn |first=Luke |title=How Tyler Dorsey, a California native, came to star for Greece's U19 team |url=https://www.si.com/college/2015/07/09/tyler-dorsey-oregon-ducks-greece-u19s |access-date=2022-09-15 |magazine=Sports Illustrated |date=July 9, 2015 }} He turned out to be a vital addition to the team, as he went on to record 15.9 [[Point (basketball)|points]] and 5.0 [[Rebound (basketball)|rebounds]] per game, and also lead the team in minutes played. The Greek team went 5–2. After winning their first 5 games, they fell to the [[USA national under-19 basketball team|USA]] in a tight semi-final, and later lost in the bronze medal game to [[Turkey men's national under-18 and under-19 basketball team|Turkey]]. He was voted onto the tournament's best team, despite his team not earning a spot on the medals podium. ===Greek senior national team=== On June 6, 2016, Dorsey was named to the senior men's [[Greek national basketball team]]'s 16-man preliminary training camp roster for the [[2016 FIBA World Olympic Qualifying Tournament – Turin|2016 Turin FIBA World Olympic qualifying tournament]]. He played with the senior team in 3 [[exhibition games|friendly]] games, however, he did not make the actual 12-man roster that would compete at the tournament.{{Cite web|url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/featured/272199/greek-nt-squad-for-oqt-is-announced/|title=Greek NT squad for OQT is announced|date=July 1, 2016|website=Eurohoops.net}} Dorsey played for Greece at the [[2019 FIBA Basketball World Cup qualification (Europe)|2019 FIBA World Cup qualification]]. He appeared in two friendly games against France and Montenegro, and appeared in two qualification games against Georgia and Serbia.{{cite web |title=Game by game stats for Tyler Dorsey - 2018-2019 Season |url=https://www.proballers.com/basketball/player/66909/tyler-dorsey/games/2018 |website=Proballers.com |access-date=09/05/2026}} Dorsey was on Greece's roster for [[EuroBasket 2022]]. On September 2, he scored 27 points in a 89–85 opening day win over [[Croatia men's national basketball team|Croatia]].{{Cite web |title=Clutch Giannis Antetokounmpo fires Greece to win over Croatia |url=https://basketnews.com/news-177303-clutch-giannis-antetokounmpo-fires-greece-to-win-over-croatia.html |access-date=2022-09-06 |website=Basketnews.com |language=en}} Dorsey returned to Greece for [[EuroBasket 2025|Eurobasket 2025]]. He averaged 12.6 points per game, 2.8 rebounds, and 2.1 assists on 44% shooting.{{Cite web|url=https://www.fiba.basketball/en/events/fiba-eurobasket-2025/teams/greece/217865-tyler-dorsey|title=Tyler Dorsey - Greece - Player Profile - FIBA EuroBasket 2025 | FIBA Basketball|website=Fiba.basketball}} Dorsey played a key role as Greece finished in 3rd place, earning a spot on the medal podium for the first time at a major tournament since 2009.{{Cite web |title= Dorsey: "This is Greek fashion. We can't finish the game smoothly"|date=September 14, 2025 |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/eurobasket/1868572/tyler-dorsey-talks-bronze-medal-greece-eurobasket-2025-fiba/#google_vignette|website=Eurohoops.net}} Dorsey finished the tournament as Greece’s second leading scorer, behind [[Giannis Antetokounmpo]].{{Cite web |title= Greece Team Profile - FIBA EuroBasket 2025 | FIBA Basketball|date=September 15, 2025 |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/en/events/fiba-eurobasket-2025/teams/greece|website=Fiba.basketball}} Dorsey played for Greece at the [[2027 FIBA Basketball World Cup qualification (Europe)|2027 FIBA World Cup Qualification]]. He appeared in two friendly games vs Poland and Cyprus, and two qualification games vs Spain and Ukraine. On August 31st 2026 vs Spain, he scored 29 points and made several clutch shots leading Greece to a thrilling 108-106 overtime win.{{cite web |title=World Cup 2027 European Qualifiers: Greece Edge Spain in Overtime Thriller Behind Mitoglou and Dorsey |url=https://www.eurobasket.com/Greece/news/1026464/World-Cup-2027-European-Qualifiers-Greece-Edge-Spain-in-Overtime-Thriller-Behind-Mitoglou-and-Dorsey |website=EuroBasket News
